question: Which body part is mainly responsible for exchanging heat with the outside environment?
explanation: The skin acts as the main boundary between the body and the outside environment, helping to balance body heat. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is keeping the body temperature around 37°C so important?

options.A: It prevents all forms of physical fatigue
options.B: It protects vital organs from extreme temperatures
options.C: It increases red blood cell destruction
options.D: It stops the production of waste products

explanation: A stable core temperature ensures cells work properly and protects internal organs from damage caused by extreme heat or cold. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which skin gland produces a watery fluid that cools the body when it evaporates?
explanation: Eccrine sweat glands release watery fluid onto the skin surface, which absorbs body heat and cools you down as it evaporates. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the main job of the fat layer under the skin (subcutaneous fat) when you are exposed to cold?

options.A: Opening blood vessels to let out trapped heat
options.B: Producing sweat to cool the skin
options.C: Providing insulation to keep heat from escaping the body

explanation: Subcutaneous fat acts as an insulating layer that slows down how fast body heat escapes into the cold air. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which part of the brain acts as the body's main thermostat?
explanation: The hypothalamus contains the control center that monitors temperature changes and tells the body how to respond. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h3)

question: Where does the hypothalamus get temperature information from?

options.A: The outer layer of the epidermis only
options.B: Receptors in the skin and inside the core
options.C: Skeletal muscles and bone marrow only

explanation: To keep body temperature balanced, the hypothalamus continuously receives signals from both surface skin receptors and internal core organs. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h3)

question: What happens to blood vessels in the skin when the body needs to lose extra heat?
explanation: Vasodilation widens surface blood vessels, bringing warm blood closer to the skin so the heat can escape into the air. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h4)

question: How does sweat on the skin help cool the body down?

options.A: Fluid secretion directly lowers blood temperature
options.B: Sweat creates an insulating layer against warmth
options.C: Heat is drawn away from the body as the moisture evaporates
options.D: Moisture reacts with fat to make cold energy

explanation: As sweat changes from liquid to vapor, it absorbs and removes thermal energy from the skin surface. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the term for rapid, involuntary muscle contractions that generate heat when you are cold?
explanation: Shivering makes skeletal muscles work quickly, turning chemical energy into body heat. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why does narrowing of skin blood vessels (vasoconstriction) help you survive in the cold?

options.B: It keeps warm blood deep inside the core away from the cold skin
options.C: It rushes blood to fingers and toes to stop freezing

explanation: By narrowing surface blood vessels, the body keeps warm blood near vital internal organs and reduces heat loss. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the medical term for a core body temperature that drops dangerously below 35°C?
explanation: Hypothermia happens when the core body temperature falls below normal operating limits, which is generally under 35°C. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h6)

question: What primary environmental factor contributes to the development of heat stroke in high temperatures?

options.A: Excessive shivering caused by sudden drafts
options.B: Sudden vasodilation of deep core blood vessels
options.C: Rapid increase in subcutaneous adipose tissue insulation
options.D: High humidity that prevents effective sweat evaporation

explanation: High ambient humidity stops sweat from evaporating off the skin, trapping heat inside the body and causing core temperatures to rise rapidly. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T4#GNS211_U2_T4_h6)
